title: Batch action-view projection

effect.user: Queued actions expose current predecessor holds without repeatedly scanning their lane.
assertions: Exact single-row projection parity, including filtered reads and mixed statuses.
Hold priority, cancelled skipping, order and token omission remain unchanged.
Controls, audit replay and reopen stay consistent.
exclusions: Wall-clock latency, CPU, RSS, fsync and whole-daemon cost

repeated.why: Three repetitions of each query shape.

background.why: No renderer or runtime is launched.

release.why: Fixture stores close; memory is not measured.

recovery.why: Separate test reopens persisted rows and verifies current views.

fixture.seed: temporary SQLite stores; queued/paused/mixed/filtered/terminal status shapes

recipe.readiness: Fixture rows installed; expected views and state recorded before counters.
recipe.completion: One listActionViews call per scenario/size/round, exact output and state comparison.
recipe.warmup: None; deterministic operation counts, no timing.
recipe.teardown: Close fixture stores and remove their temporary directories.

metrics.scope: Full-lane numeric element reads per stored action during one listActionViews query
metrics.collector: Proxy around per-instance listActionsOf results in action-views.test.ts; setup excluded
metrics.invariant: All 45 retained samples have exact view parity and at most four lane element reads per stored row.
metrics.noise: Deterministic counts; three repetitions per scenario/size. No latency interpretation.

gaps: Single actionView and scheduling retain their current scans.
SQL queries, parsing, allocations and whole-daemon latency are outside this count.
256-row lanes are a synthetic scaling control, not observed production prevalence.
readiness: 45 count samples with exact view parity; 47 tests including filtered controls/reopen and exhaustive ordered status combinations. No CPU, latency or memory claim.
